title: An archive member names its own destination path, and the extractor joins it onto the target directory
index_line: T-0057 · FILE_WRITE · a crafted member path escapes the extraction root, into a folder something runs from · c/any-archiver · corroborated
invariant_violated: Extraction is assumed to be a reproduction: the archive's paths are its content, so writing them out faithfully is the feature. But a member path is attacker-authored data, and joining it onto the chosen directory lets it walk out. The archive is a delivery vehicle whose payload is a path, so content scanning never sees it.

mechanism.does: the attacker builds an archive whose member names contain traversal or absolute components
the extractor parses the member table and takes each stored path as the destination
the member path is joined onto the extraction directory, and dot segments or a drive/root prefix resolve as written
the file is written outside the target directory, typically into a startup or auto-load location
the payload runs at next logon or next service start, with no further attacker action

source.file.name.value: the member path inside the archive — the user opens the container, the path inside it is the weapon

fs.path.join.value: the join of extraction root with member name; the reset and dot-segment semantics decide whether it escapes

encoding.path.value: dot segments, absolute paths, drive-relative prefixes, and separator variants

sink.file.write.value: the extraction write; the destination is the payload

preconditions.expr: the extractor honours member paths without confining them

check.spec: extract a test archive with a traversing member and see where the file lands

preconditions.expr: a writable location outside the target directory is useful to the attacker (startup folder, plugin dir, cron)
the user can be induced to open the archive

spec.method: confirm the delivery vector and that no warning fires for the container itself

success: a file appears outside the directory the user chose for extraction
the escaped file sits in a location that executes at logon or service start
the archive's member table shows the traversal — the container looks benign to content scanners
failure_like: member paths are canonicalised and rejected when they leave the root
extraction is sandboxed with the destination read-only outside the target
false_positive: a file with dot segments in its name that stays inside the root after canonicalisation
a rejected traversal: confirm the file did not land, not that the request succeeded

hazards: zip-slip applies to every unpacker: archive, backup restore, package deploy, container image layer, plugin install
detection has to look inside the container — an attachment scanner reading bytes sees no payload
the escape only matters because of where it writes; enumerate writable auto-load locations per platform before claiming impact

related to T-0006 (a request parameter joined onto a base): there the escape comes from a parameter, here from the container's own structure, and the fix differs — reject the member rather than normalise the join
non_transfers: extractors that reject absolute and traversing member names, or write via handles opened relative to a directory
sandboxed extraction with a read-only destination

provenance.corroborates: the flaw in handling of file paths within archives, traversal to unintended directories, and the fixed release

provenance.author: SecPod research on CVE-2025-6218 and APT-C-08
provenance.corroborates: independent exploitation analysis of the traversal-to-startup-folder chain
